gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Apple TV 4K's wired port tops out at Gigabit (and the 64 GB Wi-Fi-only 3rd-generation model has no Ethernet port at all), so a 2.5GbE NAS adds nothing for Infuse. None of them says that Infuse supports only Dolby Vision Profiles 5 and 8, so UHD Blu-ray remuxes (Profile 7) fall back to HDR whichever NAS serves them.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited (Firecore's 'Streaming From a Mac, PC, or NAS' and firecore.com/infuse) and its answer. The Firecore support article lists the SMB modes (Auto/SMB3/SMB2/SMB1/Legacy) and protocols but says nothing about Ethernet, bandwidth or NAS brands. firecore.com/infuse lists 'Dolby Vision (Profile 5 & 8)' but never says that disc remuxes are Profile 7 or what happens to them. ChatGPT's answer says 'SMB + Gigabit Ethernet' is enough but gives no reason, and it does not name the Apple TV's port limit or the Wi-Fi-only model with no port. None of the pages says Dolby Vision and Atmos need Infuse Pro, beyond the feature list on firecore.com.
decides: It backs the cheapest 1GbE pick (Synology DS124 at 1×1GbE, or UGREEN DH2300 at $239.99) over 2.5GbE boxes such as the DXP2800 or Asustor AS1102TL, because the Apple TV's own port is Gigabit and Camera Jabber measured the DH2300 at 109 MB/s (about 872 Mb/s) wired. It adds two warnings that apply whatever NAS is bought: shoppers with the 64 GB Wi-Fi-only Apple TV 4K (3rd gen) are limited to Wi-Fi, and Profile 7 remuxes will play as HDR10, not Dolby Vision, so a transcoding NAS will not fix that.
